source_title: Trump's 'Winter White House', airport get air defence systems amid Iran war fears
source_excerpt:
While the US Secret Service, which guards the President, called it 'another layer of security', the timing of the move has raised concerns about a possible escalation in the Iran conflict.
New surface-to-air missile systems have been deployed at US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago golf estate in Florida and near the Trump International Airport in West Palm Beach amid fears of a new round of heavy combat operations against Iran. While the US Secret Service, which guards the President, called it "another layer of security", the timing of the move has raised concerns about a possible escalation in the Middle East turmoil.
A pair of Avenger Air Defence Systems have been stationed on a floating barge in the Lake Worth Lagoon on the west side of Trump's sprawling 17-acre oceanfront property, which he once called the 'Winter White House'. It was first spotted by a photojournalist from the Palm Beach Daily last week, shortly before Trump arrived at the golf estate.
Separately, another set of air missile systems has been positioned on the southern side of the Donald J. Trump International Airport, close to the area where Air Force One is parked during the President's visits. WHAT ARE AVENGER MISSILE SYSTEMS?
The Avengers are short-range air defence systems that are mounted on Humvee military vehicles. The systems are designed to fire surface-to-air missiles at aircraft, drones and other aerial threats. They can be operated by a two-person crew and can even fire while on the move.
The deployment near Mar-a-Lago is significant because the system provides a ground-based layer of protection against aerial threats. However, the Avengers cannot intercept long-range missiles or ballistic ones.
Instead, it is meant to tackle threats flying at lower altitudes.
Aviation experts told WPTV that the missile systems are intended as a last line of defence. Analyst Dewitt Ingram described the weapons as a final layer of protection behind fighter jets and other measures.
The deployments come amid plans to permanently lock down the airspace over Mar-a-Lago.
Since Trump returned to the White House last year, the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) has said it intercepted more than 60 aircraft near Trump's Florida estate.
On October 24, an F-16 fighter jet intercepted an aircraft that violated the restricted airspace near Mar-a-Lago.
Both NORAD and the US Northern Command confirmed the deployment of the missile systems. However, they did not specify if a particular threat was behind the sudden deployments.
"At the request of the US Secret Service... NORAD and USNORTHCOM deployed ground-based air defence assets in and around Mar-a-Lago, Florida. Due to security considerations, we cannot provide tactics, techniques and procedural specifics," NORAD said in a statement. WHAT DO THE DEPLOYMENTS SUGGEST?
The deployment comes against the backdrop of growing indications that the US and Israel could be preparing for another major military confrontation with Iran after the midterm elections next week.
US Senator Chris Murphy recently said a handful of officials have been briefed on the proposed war plan, which he dubbed "insane".
"Some of us have been briefed on the war plan. And while I cannot disclose any details, I can say this: the plan is insane. It will not achieve objectives and will set off a new cycle of escalation," Murphy said.
According to a report in the Washington Post, the Trump administration has asked several Gulf countries to be prepared for a short but intense military campaign after the November 3 midterm elections.
Separately, the US military has put in motion a new initiave called FORTRESS . It entails preparing for a scenario in which its military bases could run for 90 days without external support in the face of any disruptions to power grids and other supply chains.
It is among the several indications that suggest the US and Israel are weighing a fresh round of strikes against Iran. Last week, we mentioned some of the signals that indicate the Middle East could be heading for another military showdown - Ends
